_comment: KCD:MP dedicated server. Import into a Pterodactyl 1.x panel (PTDL_v2). Community-made by ewbree (Redmiles); not affiliated with the KCD:MP project.
name: KCD:MP
author: ewbree@users.noreply.github.com
description: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II multiplayer server. Runs the framework-dependent .NET 10 server from the archive's linux/ folder, downloading it from the official GitHub releases on the first start and keeping it current on later starts when auto-update is on. Ports are rendered into server.toml on the first start; the panel's variables for admins, the public list, the audit and the game mode's database are passed straight to the server as its KCDMP_* environment variables.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
set -e
cd /mnt/server

# The server files come from the official GitHub releases. With AUTO_UPDATE=1
# the first start downloads them; uploading the archive's linux/ folder over
# SFTP works too, and is the way to supply custom files or a pinned build.
if [ ! -f KcdMp.Server ]; then
  echo "KcdMp.Server is not here yet: AUTO_UPDATE=1 downloads it on the first start, or upload the archive's linux/ folder over SFTP."
fi

chmod +x KcdMp.Server 2>/dev/null || true
mkdir -p data gamemodes

# Files created by this root-owned installer must belong to the unprivileged
# container user afterwards, or the server cannot write data/ or server.log.
id -u container >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -m -d /home/container container
chown -R container:container /mnt/server

echo "install complete: start the server to download or update the files, or upload them over SFTP"

variables.name: Server name
variables.description: What players see in the launcher and on the public list.

variables.name: Password
variables.description: Players must send this to join. Empty means the server is open to anyone.

variables.name: Max players
variables.description: Slot count. Player ids run from 0 to this minus one. Roughly a tenth of a core and 1.5 MB/s outbound per fifty players moving and fighting at once.

variables.name: Game mode script
variables.description: Path to the .lua script or compiled .dll, relative to the server folder. Empty uses the built-in freeroam mode.

variables.name: Admins
variables.description: Comma-separated player names the freeroam mode promotes to admin, e.g. Henry,Hans. Sets KCDMP_ADMINS.

variables.name: Master list URL
variables.description: The public server list the server announces itself to. Empty keeps the server private: it appears nowhere and players join by direct connect. Set to https://kcd-mp.com/server-list to publish it. Sets KCDMP_MASTER_URL and overrides [master] url in server.toml.

variables.name: Audit mode
variables.description: observe only logs what the item and progression checks would do; enforce takes unexplained items away. Sets KCDMP_AUDIT_MODE and overrides [audit] mode in server.toml. Start with observe and read the log first.

variables.name: Database driver
variables.description: The game mode's own database, on the panel's MySQL/MariaDB or PostgreSQL server. Empty means no database. Sets KCDMP_DB_DRIVER.

variables.name: Database URL
variables.description: One line instead of host, port, user, password and name: mysql://user:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/kcdmp. Sets KCDMP_DB_URL. Credentials live in this panel variable, never in a game mode script.

variables.name: Extra TOML
variables.description: Appended verbatim to the generated server.toml on the first start. Use it for keys the panel does not expose, e.g. a [rates] or [world] section. Existing keys are not merged: an appended table with a key already set above makes the file invalid TOML.

variables.name: Regenerate server.toml
variables.description: 0 keeps an existing server.toml forever, so edits made in the file manager survive restarts. 1 rewrites it from these variables on every start, discarding those edits. Set it back to 0 after one restart unless you want the panel to own the whole file.

variables.name: Auto-update server files
variables.description: 1 checks the official GitHub releases on every start and installs the newest build if it differs from the files on disk. 0 never contacts GitHub and leaves the files alone. Turn it off if you run a custom compiled game mode or a patched binary. server.toml, data/ and your own game modes are never overwritten.

variables.name: Server version
variables.description: latest follows the newest release. A version such as 0.50.0 pins it: with auto-update on the server moves to exactly that release, including a downgrade, which is the way back if a new release breaks your game mode. With auto-update off this has no effect.

variables.name: GitHub token
variables.description: Optional, and only used to read release metadata and download the archive. Raises GitHub's anonymous limit of 60 requests an hour per IP, which a node running many servers can reach. A fine-grained token with no scopes is enough.
